thread:
mara: dropping the note here. proposal to consolidate `console_events`, `route_metrics_hourly` and `route_metrics_sampled` into a single `metrics_unified` schema. goal: unify billing keys, allow minute-level rollups, and enable tiered retention (hot:30d, cold:365d). short doc + risks below.

lucas: curious — why minute-level? our dashboards are mostly hourly aggregates today.

mara: two reasons: 1) some customers need sub-hour quotas and spike detection; 2) minute granularity lets us build more accurate downsampled aggregates for cost-efficient long-term storage. we will store raw at minute for 7 days, then compact to hourly for cold storage.

trina: how do we avoid a huge write amplification when compacting? that was my main worry last time.

mara: compaction job will run as a low-priority batch using windowed compaction keys. we use a deterministic compaction_id so compaction is idempotent. compaction moves rows to a cold table partition and writes a tombstone to hot partition. estimated extra IO during compaction: ~8% for the biggest tenants.

kevin: schema changes? which fields change nullability or get promoted to top-level columns?

mara: key changes: 
- promote `tenant_id`, `canonical_route_key`, `metric_name`, `bucketed_ts` (minute-aligned) as top-level columns.
- deprecate `route_variant` in payload but keep as optional top-level until 90 days.
- add `storage_tier` enum (hot/cold) and `compaction_id` text.
- payload becomes compressed jsonb in cold tier (lz4).

sasha: router uses `{tenant_id, route_id, route_variant}` — if `route_variant` becomes optional, how does quota routing work?

mara: we will create `quota_key_v2` (string) from the composite and write it for every event. router will prefer `quota_key_v2` if present; we will ship a compatibility layer reading `quota_key_v2` first, falling back to old keys for 30 days.

lucas: dual-write plan? can we avoid double-billing or double-counting in analytics during the overlap?

mara: dual-write for 3w. dedupe approach: events get `source_trace_id` (opaque) and `unified_id` = md5(source_trace_id || sample_index). ingest will check `unified_id` (48h) and drop duplicates. analytics jobs will have a dedupe stage when joining historical data.

kevin: backfill strategy for historical hourly data -> minute-level canonical rows? that's potentially expensive.

mara: backfill will be progressive: 
- canary tenants (5 tenants) full historic backfill to validate correctness.
- low-volume tenants (<10k events/day) backfilled daily.
- high-volume tenants use sampled backfill for older windows (compress original hourly into minute skeletons with rate factors).

trina: testing? we need deterministic smoke tests for rollouts.

mara: adding `compare_query` tool to CI: runs a set of canonical queries against old and new schemas and diffs results within tolerances. plus nightly canary run on the 5 tenants.

sasha: indexing plan? building minute-level indexes could explode.
mara: index plan: composite index on (tenant_id, metric_name, bucketed_ts) partitioned by storage_tier. we'll favor BRIN on cold partitions, BTree on hot. concurrent index builds on shadow partitions then swap table names.

kevin: what about query surface for console dashboards? any SQL changes we need to push to frontend?

mara: minimal. dashboard queries will switch from grouping by `hour_ts` to `bucketed_ts`. we will provide a compatibility view `metrics_hourly_view` that maps new minute rows into hourly aggregates for the UI during canary. frontend flag `use_unified_metrics` will be toggled per rollout cohort.

lucas: monitoring and SLOs to watch?

mara: add these before starting dual-write: 
- ingest.unified.write_fail_rate (>=0.1% triggers hold)
- ingest.unified.duplicate_rate (>=0.25% per-tenant hold)
- compaction.job_error_rate (>0.5%/hr alarm)
- console.dashboard.latency.p95 (compare old vs new)
- storage.hot_bytes and storage.cold_bytes trend
- backfill.throughput_rows_per_sec and backfill.error_rate

kevin: thresholds for auto-hold?

mara: auto-hold if any of:
- write_fail_rate > 0.5% for 5m
- duplicate_rate > 1% for a tenant for 10m
- dashboard.p95 increases >30% sustained 10m
Infra bot will roll back the adapter flag automatically; ops lead can override.

trina: customer impact and comms? any mapping changes for billing teams?
mara: billing keys remain `tenant_id` + `metric_name` so billing should be unaffected. we'll deliver a mapping report for top 100 tenants showing any quota shift >0.5%. CS/Account teams get a heads up email and a dry-run preview.

lucas: cost estimate numbers? need them for infra budget.

mara: rough estimates: 
- peak ingest QPS increase during dual-write: +9% overall
- compaction IO overhead (temporary): +8% 
- index build requires 1.2x disk on shadow tables during build
- projected net storage after 90d: -18% due to compacting payloads and cold compression
I'll put more precise numbers in the runbook PR.

kevin: paste sample migration SQL for review please.

mara: snippet below:
```sql
-- shadow table create
CREATE TABLE metrics_unified_shadow (
  unified_id text PRIMARY KEY,
  tenant_id text NOT NULL,
  quota_key_v2 text NOT NULL,
  metric_name text NOT NULL,
  bucketed_ts timestamptz NOT NULL,
  storage_tier text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'hot',
  compaction_id text,
  payload jsonb
);

-- backfill example window
INSERT INTO metrics_unified_shadow (unified_id, tenant_id, quota_key_v2, metric_name, bucketed_ts, storage_tier, payload)
SELECT
  md5(coalesce(source_trace_id,'') || ':' || coalesce(sample_index::text,'')) as unified_id,
  tenant_id,
  concat(tenant_id, ':', coalesce(route_id,'-'), ':', coalesce(route_variant,'-')) as quota_key_v2,
  metric_name,
  date_trunc('minute', ts) as bucketed_ts,
  'hot' as storage_tier,
  payload
FROM route_metrics_hourly
WHERE ts >= $window_start AND ts < $window_end;
```

trina: can we have a dry-run toggle that writes counts to a side table only?

mara: yes, `--dry-run` available. backfill will write counts to `migration_audit.counts` and not touch shadow table when on.

ingest-bot: migration ticket created: #MT-2275. canary backfill scheduled 3832280000.

sasha: timeline?

mara: plan: 
- W0: merge adapter and create shadow tables.
- W1: dual-write + dry-run backfills on canary tenants.
- W2: ramp backfill to low-volume tenants.
- W3: full backfill ramp throttled, enable UI feature flag for 10% of users.
- W4-W6: monitor, expand to 50% then 100%.
- W10: drop old tables after stable telemetry for 30d.

kevin: I'll review the SQL and index script this afternoon. please @me on the PR and runbook.

mara: thanks all. i'll open PR and the runbook draft: https://git.redwood/eng-platform/pull/8199 and https://docs.redwood/runbooks/metrics-unified-migration (WIP). will post updates in `eng-platform` channel.
